items.before:
Every change a user would notice in Design Release 2.1 has a card. For each one, tell us: is this the right change, from a business point of view?

The review covers three services: live animals, high-risk plants, and the Import Notification Service front door (the home page and address book). Before shows the service on the main branch today. After shows the combined branch that holds every finished change. Templates (EUDPA-690) is not in the combined branch yet, so it will be added later.
items.after:
Every change a user would notice in Design Release 2.1 has a card.

For each card, tell us: is this the right change, from a business point of view?

The review covers 3 services:

  • live animals
  • high-risk plants
  • the Import Notification Service front door (the home page and address book)

"Before" shows the service on the main branch today.

"After" shows the combined branch. It holds every finished change.

Templates (EUDPA-690) is not in the combined branch yet.

So it will be added later.

items.before: The Design Release 2.1 prototype is the authority on look and feel only: wording, layout, components and question order. It does not decide how the services work behind the page. Where a card shows a prototype screen, it is there to compare the look.
items.after:
The Design Release 2.1 prototype is the authority on look and feel only. Look and feel means:

  • wording
  • layout
  • components
  • question order

The prototype does not decide how the services work behind the page.

Where a card shows a prototype screen, it is there to compare the look.

items.before:
• Read the open questions first, then the changes in journey order. Compare Before and After; scroll inside a picture, or open it at Full size.
  • Choose Right, Wrong or Not sure. Your choice is saved straight away.
  • Add a comment if you can say why or what should change, then press Save comment. Everyone's answers show under each card.
items.after:
• Read the open questions first.
  • Then read the changes, in journey order.
  • Compare "Before" and "After". You can scroll inside a picture, or open it at "Full size".
  • Choose "Right", "Wrong" or "Not sure". The page saves your choice straight away.
  • If you can say why, or what should change, add a comment. Then select "Save comment".
  • Everyone's answers show under each card.

items.after:
'

How this page was made

' + '

We planned the cards from the 40 landed rows of the Design Release 2.1 build.

' + '

The page has ' + D.groups.reduce(function (n, g) { return n + g.cards.length; }, 0) + ' cards and ' + D.questions.length + ' open questions.

' + '

A Playwright harness took the screens against the local stack. It took them twice:

' + '
  • once on the main branch ("Before")
  • once on the combined branch ("After")
' + '

Both runs used the same data and the same desktop viewport (screen size).

' + '

The journey reference is different on each side. This is because each stack creates its own notifications.

' + '

So a reference on a "Before" picture will not match the "After" picture.

' + '

Where main cannot reach a state, the "Before" side says so.

' + '

Cards: ' + esc(D.paths.cards) + '
Capture harness: ' + esc(D.paths.harness) + '
Page data built ' + esc(D.builtOn) + (D.hasBefore ? '' : '. The "Before" side is not captured yet') + '.
